caption:
ThePrint's ground report on India's $250-billion IT sector put the billable hour on trial. Xpheno's Kamal Karanth makes the contrarian case: the cuts trace to margin pressure, not machines. The debate is unsettled. Your position in it is not.

Look honestly at your week. Coordination. Routing. Summarising. Status decks that restate what everyone already knows. That work is being repriced, and no amount of seniority argues with a spreadsheet.

What does not reprice is judgment delivered live, in a room, under pressure, with your name on it. The call made when the data runs out. The silence held while three people wait for you to speak. Bearing that holds when the question turns hostile.

Thirty-five years of command teaches one thing above all: authority is not conferred by title or output volume. It is demonstrated in the moment it is tested.

Build the part of your work a model cannot sit in the room and do.

topic.title: AI repricing the billable hour — what stays human
topic.angle: Lumina's managers and senior professionals do work that looks like coordination, routing and summarising, so the repricing of an hour becomes an identity question whose honest answer is judgment delivered live in a room — exactly the Lumina Method's territory.
topic.why_now: ThePrint's ground report on India's $250-billion IT sector published roughly seven days ago, and its margin-pressure-vs-AI debate (Xpheno's Kamal Karanth arguing cuts trace to margins, not machines) is still live and unsettled, opening a contrarian lane against the prevailing AI-panic leadership content.

rationale: A stark, text-only visual matches the caption's plainspoken argument that command presence is stated and demonstrated, not decorated.
